To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the LHC may discover the MSSM Higgs boson in the gluon fusion channel with a mass as high as 1.5 TeV, and that the LHC will be able to determine the mass of this Higgs boson with a precision of about 100 GeV.

the CEDP at the LHC can provide the following: a) a discovery reach for the Higgs bosons of up to 1 TeV, and b) the possibility to determine the Higgs bosonic couplings, including the trilinear Higgs self-coupling, with an accuracy of up to 10%, which is comparable with the precision that can be achieved at a future linear e+e- collider.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new approach for studying the Higgs physics at the LHC and beyond.
the study of Higgs production in CEDP at the LHC, with the aim to extend the LHC Higgs discovery potential by proton tagging.
a new approach of using CEDP for the study of the MSSM Higgs boson at the LHC, which is expected to provide a significant increase in the discovery reach of the LHC for this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, if a Higgs signal is found, it should be possible to establish the nature of the Higgs particle and its couplings to the gauge bosons and to the top quark, even if the Higgs bosons is light and the LHC is running in the low-luminosity mode.
the Higgs sector can be explored in the MSSM in a large part of the parameter space, and the CEDP can play a decisive role.
CEDP at the LHC may be an important and complementary source for the study of the MSSM Higgs sector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CEDP can significantly extend our knowledge of the Higgs couplings to the gluons and to the top quarks.
the Higgs sector of the MSSM can be probed at the LHC with unprecedented accuracy by combining the information from the central and the forward regions of the detector.
, with the CEDP at 14 TeV and with a luminosity of 300 fb-1, one can explore a wide region of the parameter space of the MSSM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CEDP can be used to probe the Higgs sector in the mass range 120–150 GeV, where the SM Higgs boson has not been found.
the CEDP can be used to measure the Higgs couplings to the top and bottom quarks, the tau-lepton and the gluon.
the Higgs sector can be explored at the LHC in the CEDP region of phase space with a sensitivity that is comparable to the SM Higgs production cross-section in the inclusive channel.
